recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. Any independent cleanup of example values or migration details should be handled under a separate tracker, because FHIR-13157's approved rate-type coverage and dosage-text clarification are already present.
issue_request: FHIR-13157 asked why a simple MedicationRequest infusion rate such as 100 ml/hr used rateRatio instead of rateSimpleQuantity/rateQuantity and asked for clearer wording about the relationship between free-text dosage instructions and structured dosage data. The final Published resolution was to create examples for all three rate[x] forms--rateRatio, rateRange, and rateQuantity--and add overview wording about free-text dosage instructions.
initial_application: The Jira comments cite an August 17, 2017 dosing-clarification application and an August 21, 2017 example/rate guidance update. Git history confirms commit 17795bbfaf5fb47e4c1961e386c5fea10e7b4926 added MedicationRequest dosage-instruction notes for FHIR-13157, while commit 485e4881046bcb3b7f45ac130fc7641bbd2bf969 converted medicationrequest0319 from rateRatio to rateQuantity, labeled the MedicationRequest examples by rate type, and added Dosage.doseAndRate.rate[x] guidance explaining that 100 ml/hour can be represented using either rateRatio or rateQuantity.
additional_context: MedicationRequest is an active resource in source/fhir.ini. Current source lists MedicationRequest examples for rateRange, rateRatio, and rateQuantity, including the FHIR-13157 rateQuantity example and later FHIR-14111 weight-based rateQuantity examples. Later Pharmacy decisions FHIR-13222 and FHIR-39319 refined Dosage.text guidance; the current model uses DosageDetails.renderedInstruction and Dosage.text to preserve the substantive rule that human-readable instructions should be complete and aligned with structured dosage data.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The modified resolution is already implemented in current build-scope source, and changing the remaining rateRatio example to rateQuantity would undercut the approved three-rate-type example coverage.
